summary_paragraph: Mr. Meléndez, a man with chronic systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and a history of heavy alcohol use, was admitted with severe right upper quadrant abdominal pain, hematemesis, and chest pain after consuming two pints of vodka. His symptoms were attributed to alcoholic gastritis with hemorrhage and alcohol withdrawal, with no evidence of acute abdominal pathology on CT or ultrasound. He was managed with high-dose omeprazole, a lidocaine patch for pain, and Zofran for nausea, which resolved during the stay. He received enoxaparin for anticoagulation, started on metoprolol for heart rate control, and was treated with Bactrim for a right axillary skin infection. He remained stable, abstinent from alcohol during admission, and was discharged home with medication adjustments, follow-up plans, and counseling on alcohol cessation.
